intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that Wolfram syndrome 2 (WFS2) is caused by homozygous mutation in the CISD2 gene (611507) on chromosome 4q24.

paragraphs.text: Wolfram syndrome 2 is an autosomal recessive disorder that includes insulin-dependent diabetes mellitus and visual impairment due to optic nerve involvement. Unlike the classic Wolfram syndrome, patients do not have diabetes insipidus. Several patients have had profound upper gastrointestinal ulceration and bleeding (El-Shanti et al., 2000), and a defect in platelet aggregation has been reported (Mozzillo et al., 2014).

checks.claim: Wolfram syndrome 2 is an autosomal recessive disorder.
checks.evidence_quote: Wolfram syndrome (WFS; MIM 222300) is a rare neurodegenerative disease with autosomal recessive inheritance and incomplete penetrance
checks.explanation: Stated for WFS generally, with WFS2 described as a type; homozygous patient with carrier parents is consistent.

checks.claim: Wolfram syndrome 2 includes insulin-dependent diabetes mellitus.
checks.evidence_quote: only insulin-dependent diabetes mellitus and optic atrophy are necessary to make the diagnosis
checks.explanation: The patients have the Wolfram syndrome phenotype, which requires IDDM for diagnosis.

checks.evidence_quote: only insulin-dependent diabetes mellitus and optic atrophy are necessary to make the diagnosis

paragraphs.text: Mozzillo et al. (2014) reported a 17-year-old Italian girl whose parents said they were not consanguineous. She had recurrent bleeding upper intestinal ulcers from age 5 years. At age 14 years she was diagnosed with malrotation and partial duodenal intussusception, which required duodenal resection. At age 16 she developed reduced visual acuity and dyschromatopsia with optic disc pallor, and at age 17 she developed non-autoimmune diabetes requiring insulin. She also had bilateral high-frequency sensorineural hearing loss and slow intestinal transit with entero-gastric bile reflux. Eye examination showed slight optic disc pallor with preserved pupillary light reflexes. Pattern VEPs were normal, and brain MRI showed normal optic nerve caliber. Visual field, ERG, microperimetry, and OCT testing showed moderate bilateral optic nerve involvement compatible with optic neuropathy rather than optic atrophy, and the findings were unchanged after 5 years of follow-up. At age 22 years she had optic neuropathy with preserved visual acuity and no optic atrophy. Mozzillo et al. (2014) suggested that the ocular disease in the Jordanian WFS2 patients was probably also optic neuropathy, and that WFS2 might not be a true WFS subtype.

paragraphs.text: Mozzillo et al. (2014) found that their patient had reduced, reversible platelet aggregation in response to ADP at concentrations up to 10 micromolar, with no platelet secretion in response to ADP. Aggregation in response to collagen, epinephrine, and ristocetin was normal, and the other main coagulation tests were normal. Her heterozygous parents and brother also showed reversible ADP-induced aggregation defects without clinical signs. The authors suggested that differences in experimental conditions or between patients could explain why the Jordanian patients had a collagen aggregation defect instead.

paragraphs.text: In affected members of 3 consanguineous Jordanian families with Wolfram syndrome who had previously been shown not to have WFS1 mutations and whose disease mapped to the WFS2 locus on 4q22-q25, Amr et al. (2007) identified a homozygous G-to-C transversion at nucleotide 109 of the ZCD2 (CISD2) gene, predicting a glu37-to-gln (E37Q) substitution at a conserved residue. paragraphs.text: In an Italian girl with WFS2, Mozzillo et al. (2014) found a novel homozygous deletion of the entire CISD2 exon 2, detected because exon 2 failed to amplify by PCR and confirmed by cDNA sequencing. SNP array analysis restricted the deletion to at most 2,050 bp, extending from intron 2 to intron 3. Her parents and brother were heterozygous for the deletion. The deleted region includes the codons for amino acids 102 to 106 within the 2Fe-2S domain, and the authors suggested that the deletion would result in a nonfunctional protein. Runs-of-homozygosity analysis showed no parental relationship, but microsatellite analysis supported a common ancestor; the grandparents came from the same small Italian island.

paragraphs.text: In affected members of 3 consanguineous Jordanian families with Wolfram syndrome 2, Amr et al. (2007) identified a homozygous c.109G-C transversion in the ZCD2 (CISD2) gene, predicting a glu37-to-gln (E37Q) substitution at a conserved residue. The mutation disrupted mRNA splicing by eliminating exon 2, resulting in a premature stop codon. The authors concluded that the aberrant splicing, rather than the amino acid change, was the basis of pathogenesis.

checks.claim: Amr et al. (2007) identified a homozygous c.109G-C transversion in the ZCD2 (CISD2) gene in affected members of 3 consanguineous Jordanian families with Wolfram syndrome 2.
checks.evidence_quote: A G-->C transversion at nucleotide 109 predicts an amino acid change from glutamic acid to glutamine (E37Q).
checks.explanation: The abstract gives the variant and the three families, and the title says the mutation is homozygous.

checks.claim: The CISD2 c.109G-C transversion predicts a glu37-to-gln (E37Q) substitution.
checks.evidence_quote: A G-->C transversion at nucleotide 109 predicts an amino acid change from glutamic acid to glutamine (E37Q).

checks.claim: The CISD2 E37Q substitution affects a conserved residue.
checks.evidence_quote: Although the amino acid is conserved and the mutation is nonsynonymous

checks.claim: The CISD2 c.109G-C mutation disrupted mRNA splicing by eliminating exon 2.
checks.evidence_quote: The mutation was found to disrupt messenger RNA splicing by eliminating exon 2

checks.claim: The CISD2 c.109G-C mutation results in a premature stop codon.
checks.evidence_quote: it results in the introduction of a premature stop codon.

checks.claim: Amr et al. (2007) concluded that aberrant splicing, rather than the amino acid change, was the basis of pathogenesis of the CISD2 c.109G-C mutation.
checks.evidence_quote: the pathogenesis for the disorder is because the mutation also causes aberrant splicing.

paragraphs.text: In an Italian girl with Wolfram syndrome 2, Mozzillo et al. (2014) found a homozygous deletion of the entire CISD2 exon 2, detected because exon 2 failed to amplify by PCR and confirmed by cDNA sequencing. SNP array analysis restricted the deletion to at most 2,050 bp. Her parents and brother were heterozygous for the deletion. The deleted region includes the codons for amino acids 102 to 106 within the 2Fe-2S domain, and the authors suggested that the deletion would result in a nonfunctional protein. Microsatellite analysis supported a common ancestor, and the grandparents came from the same small Italian island.

checks.claim: Mozzillo et al. (2014) found a homozygous deletion of the entire CISD2 exon 2 in an Italian girl with Wolfram syndrome 2.
checks.evidence_quote: CISD2 cDNA sequencing revealed a novel homozygous deletion affecting the whole exon 2 of CISD2

checks.claim: The CISD2 exon 2 deletion in the Italian girl with Wolfram syndrome 2 was detected because exon 2 failed to amplify by PCR.
checks.evidence_quote: In the patient the amplification of CISD2 exon 2 was not detected, while exons 1 and 3 were regularly present.

checks.claim: The CISD2 exon 2 deletion in the Italian girl with Wolfram syndrome 2 was confirmed by cDNA sequencing.
checks.evidence_quote: CISD2 cDNA sequencing revealed a novel homozygous deletion affecting the whole exon 2 of CISD2

checks.claim: SNP array analysis restricted the CISD2 exon 2 deletion in the Italian girl with Wolfram syndrome 2 to at most 2,050 bp.
checks.evidence_quote: Combining these data with the ones from PCR, we were able to map the proximal breakpoint
checks.explanation: The 2,050 bp maximum comes from combining SNP-array and PCR data. The SNP array alone gave a maximum of 4,250 bp.

checks.claim: The parents and brother of the Italian girl with Wolfram syndrome 2 were heterozygous for the CISD2 exon 2 deletion.
checks.evidence_quote: The deletion was homozygous in the proband and heterozygous in her parents and brother.

checks.claim: The region deleted by the CISD2 exon 2 deletion includes the codons for amino acids 102 to 106 within the 2Fe-2S domain.
checks.evidence_quote: Genomic data from our subjects show that the triplets coding for aminoacids WRSKT, from the position 102 to 106 of the polypeptide, are within the deleted region
checks.explanation: The 2Fe-2S domain is stated to span residues 99-112.

checks.claim: Mozzillo et al. (2014) suggested that the CISD2 exon 2 deletion would result in a nonfunctional protein.
checks.evidence_quote: this may result in a non functional protein because of zinc-finger domain lost

checks.claim: Microsatellite analysis supported a common ancestor for the parents of the Italian girl with Wolfram syndrome 2.
checks.evidence_quote: Microsatellite analysis confirmed the hypothesis of a common ancestor (data not shown).

checks.claim: The grandparents of the Italian girl with Wolfram syndrome 2 came from the same small Italian island.
checks.evidence_quote: their grandparents were born in the same Italian small island where they are still living
